issues.legal_issue: An employee occupying premises under an employer’s housing agreement occupies as a licensee rather than a tenant when the agreement gives only a personal privilege and no interest in the land.
material_facts: The employer provided flats to officers for their convenience while employed at the relevant location.
The officer’s right to occupy ended upon termination of employment, transfer away, or death.
The employer could allot another flat to the officer and could assign the flat to another employee or suitable person during the officer’s absence.
The agreement reserved the employer’s right to levy a fee, restricted the officer’s use of the premises, and stated that it created no landlord-and-tenant relationship.
issues.conclusion: The agreement, construed according to its substance and in light of the circumstances, created a licence and not a tenancy; the officer received only a personal privilege to occupy the flat and no interest in the land.
issues.legal_principle: Under section 105 of the Transfer of Property Act, 1882, a lease transfers a right to enjoy premises; under section 52 of the Indian Easements Act, 1882, a licence is a privilege to do something on premises that would otherwise be unlawful. The substance of the transaction governs, not the parties’ label; exclusive possession is important but not decisive. A servant can be a licensee even without a service occupation. The Court relied on Errington v. Errington and Woods, Associated Hotels of India Ltd. v. R. N. Kapoor, Addiscombe Garden Estates Ltd. v. Crabbe, Nippon Menkwa Kalmshiki v. F. Portlock, and Torbett v. Faulkner.

rule.if: landlord_eviction_claim and employment_related_housing and occupancy_ends_with_employment_or_transfer_or_death and employer_controls_reallocation and agreement_confers_no_interest_in_land

predicates.landlord_eviction_claim: A landlord brought a proceeding seeking recovery of premises from an occupier.
predicates.employment_related_housing: An employer permitted an employee to occupy premises for convenience connected with the employee’s work.
predicates.occupancy_ends_with_employment_or_transf: The employee’s right to occupy ended when employment ended, the employee was transferred away, or the employee died.
predicates.employer_controls_reallocation: The employer could allot different premises to the employee or assign the premises to someone else.
predicates.agreement_confers_no_interest_in_land: The agreement gave the employee a personal privilege to occupy but no interest in the land.

issues.definition: When a landlord seeks recovery of premises and an employment-related housing agreement gives the employee only a personal privilege, ends occupancy with specified employment-related events, and leaves reallocation under the employer’s control, the occupier is a licensee.

issues.legal_issue: A landlord’s reasonable requirement for its own occupation includes premises occupied on its behalf by employees who hold them as licensees.
material_facts: The companies purchased the premises to provide residential accommodation for their staff.
One company was obliged to provide accommodation for its officers, and suitable accommodation for transferred officers and visiting officers was difficult to obtain.
The courts below found that the company reasonably required the flats for its staff.
Under the standard agreement, the officers occupied as licensees, and the parties accepted that a licensee occupied on the company’s behalf.
issues.conclusion: The company reasonably required the flats for its own occupation through officers holding them as licensees on its behalf.
issues.legal_principle: Section 13(1)(f) of the West Bengal Premises Tenancy Act, 1956 permits recovery where premises are reasonably required by the landlord for its own occupation. The Court applied the distinction between a lease and a licence under section 105 of the Transfer of Property Act, 1882 and section 52 of the Indian Easements Act, 1882, and relied on Associated Hotels of India Ltd. v. R. N. Kapoor and the other authorities cited in its discussion of that distinction. It held that occupation by employees as the landlord’s licensees is occupation on the landlord’s behalf.

predicates.landlord_eviction_claim_for_own_occupati: A landlord brought a proceeding seeking recovery of premises on the ground that it required them for its own occupation.
predicates.landlord_reasonably_requires_premises_fo: The landlord reasonably required the premises to house its staff.
predicates.staff_occupy_as_landlord_licensees: Staff members held the premises as licensees on the landlord’s behalf.

issues.definition: If a landlord seeking premises for its own occupation reasonably requires them for staff and the staff occupy as its licensees, their occupation counts as the landlord’s own occupation.
